text.tspan: Stretching over 3,000 kilometers along East Asia’s Pacific Rim,
Japan is a volcanic archipelago of 14,125 islands anchored by four
main landmasses: Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu, and Shikoku. Roughly
73% of its territory is mountainous and heavily forested, concentrating
over 124 million residents into coastal plains and interconnected
Nowhere is this concentration more pronounced than along the
Taiheiyo Belt on southern Honshu. Linked by the pioneering
Tokaido Shinkansen high-speed rail line, Japan’s four largest cities—
and cultural spine of the country.
SYNTHESIS — Over the past century, Japan transformed from an agrarian imperial society into one of the world’s most sophisticated industrial and
technological economies. Lacking abundant domestic natural resources, the nation invested heavily in human capital, precision manufacturing, high-trust
civic institutions, and dense transit infrastructure—foundations that today support unrivaled urban safety and cultural soft power even as policymakers
confront the structural headwinds of an aging society, currency realignments, and shifting global trade dynamics.

dollar amid diverging central bank interest rates.
